value: 37 of the 90 strongly responding antennal olfactory sensory neurons (A cells) responded best to the aggregation pheromone lineatin
method: single-sensillum recordings from antennal club sensilla with a 57-compound odour panel at 10 ug per stimulus, followed by dose-response series
conditions: adults field-collected April to June 2020 and 2021 with lineatin-baited funnel traps in two conifer forests in southern Sweden, so the beetles had been drawn to the compound being tested; beetles fixed in wax, compounds screened in random order, a 10 uL paraffin oil blank once per sensillum and any oil response subtracted from the net response; 'strongly responding' is defined in the Table 1 caption as 80 Hz or more to one or several compounds at the 10 ug dose, and responses under 20 Hz at the screening dose count as no response; Methods say 187 sensilla were contacted using 48 male and 64 female beetles whereas the Abstract and Results say 170 sensilla, and the paper does not reconcile the two; thirteen OSN classes were found, most in both sexes (classes 5, 8 and 11 only in males, class 7 only in females); the lineatin class held 22 female and 15 male neurons by Table 1 and the text does not test a sex difference; the next Results sentence says 28 of the lineatin-responsive neurons also responded to other compounds, generally more weakly; the dose-response series (10 pg to 10 ug, 8 neurons) gave a threshold near 10 pg and used racemic (+/-)-lineatin; the quote counts the best-responding class, not a response threshold

value: video playbacks of an attacking (frontal) predator induced responses much like a live predator
method: five stimuli (empty tank, moving square, calmly swimming predator video, attacking predator video, live predator) shown on a 25 cm by 15 cm LED tablet screen next to the focal fish tank
conditions: Experiment 1, N = 16 focal fish each given all five stimuli; focal fish were predator-naive adults 40 to 45 mm from University of Bern laboratory stock reared for five generations; predators (Lepidiolamprologus elongatus, 80 to 140 mm) were first-generation offspring of wild-caught fish; each focal fish was exposed to every cue for 5 min in randomised order with at least 3 h between presentations; behaviour video-recorded and coded in Solomon Coder by an observer blind to the cue; no exclusions of non-responders are mentioned; aggressive displays differed by presentation type (GLMM chi2 = 23.41, p = 0.0001); frontal (attack) playback did not differ from the live predator in aggressive displays (p = 0.13) but focal fish were more attentive to the live predator than to the frontal playback (p = 0.02), so 'much like' holds for aggression only; lateral (calm) playback drew much less aggression than the live predator (p = 0.0008); the page also reports no difference between lateral and frontal playbacks at p = 0.98 (Table 2) for a measure the text read does not name; the screen frame rate is not reported; the quote is the Abstract sentence

value: lowest acoustically evoked behavioral response (AEBR) thresholds of 140 to 150 dB re 1 uPa (-33 to -23 dB re 1 g) at frequencies below 225 Hz in larvae
method: behavioural startle-like caudal fin response (movement greater than half the body length) to 100 ms pure tones at 75 Hz and 105 to 425 Hz in 40 Hz steps, levels stepped down from 154 to 136 dB re 1 uPa in 3 dB steps
conditions: larvae and juveniles of 1.4 to 3.2 cm total length from eggs taken from nest rocks in the intertidal at Tamales Bay, California (spelling as returned by the page tool), and Seal Rock Beach, Washington, reared in 190 L aquaria at 15 +/- 2 C and tested after 5 min acclimation in a darkened booth, stimuli calibrated for equal sound pressure and presented in random order; threshold groups were small (n = 19, 1.5 to 1.7 cm), medium (n = 19, 1.8 to 2.4 cm), large (n = 12, 2.5 to 2.7 cm) and juvenile (n = 17, 2.8 to 3.2 cm); thresholds vary with size (MANOVA frequency F9,62 = 32.94, p < 0.001; group F3,62 = 6.41, p = 0.001) and the medium group had lower thresholds than the small group at 75 and 105 Hz (7.4 and 6.5 dB, p < 0.001); best evoked frequency ranged 75 to 145 Hz; onset experiment: 62 larvae, broadband click peak 154 dB re 1 uPa, no larva under 1.4 cm responded, 50% responded at 1.5 cm and all above 1.8 cm; no sham (no-stimulus) control is described; this is a behavioural threshold of larvae, not an adult auditory-nerve or evoked-potential audiogram; the Abstract's statement about the 1.9 to 2.4 cm group differs from the Results wording on best evoked frequency (the tool summary notes the abstract wording appears to misstate it), the quote is not affected
